name: Toolszu PDF Embedder & Viewer
author: Toolszu

sections.description:
Toolszu PDF Embedder & Viewer shows any PDF right inside your pages, so visitors can read it without downloading anything. It works on phones, tablets and computers, and it is completely free: no paid version, no locked features and no account.

The viewer

  • Smooth scrolling through every page, sharp on high-resolution screens.
  • Search inside the PDF, with highlighted matches and next/previous.
  • Zoom: automatic, page width, whole page, or 25% to 400%.
  • Page thumbnails in a side panel.
  • Full screen, including on iPhone.
  • Download, print and open in a new tab buttons. Turn any of them off.
  • Selectable text and working links inside the PDF, including links to other pages of the same PDF.
  • Password-protected PDFs ask for the password.
  • Light, dark or automatic theme, plus your own accent color.
  • Keyboard shortcuts: Page Up / Page Down, + and -, Ctrl+F to search.

Three ways to add a PDF

  • Block editor: add the “PDF Viewer” block and choose a file from the Media Library, upload one, or paste a link.
  • Any editor: paste a link to a PDF on its own line. It turns into a viewer automatically.
  • Shortcode: [toolszu_pdf id="123"] or [toolszu_pdf url="https://example.com/file.pdf"]. Every PDF in the Media Library shows its ready-to-copy shortcode.

Save as PDF for your articles

Add a “Save as PDF” button to your posts. It opens a clean copy of the article, with the title, featured image, content and a link to the original, without menus, sidebars or ads, and the browser’s print window, where readers choose “Save as PDF”. Great for recipes, guides, tutorials and documentation.
* Add it automatically to posts, pages or any public content type, before or after the content.
* Or place it yourself with the “Save as PDF Button” block or the [toolszu_save_pdf] shortcode.
* The print copy is hidden from search engines, so it never competes with your article.

Fast and private

  • The viewer loads only on pages that show a PDF, and the PDF engine loads only when the viewer scrolls into view.
  • Long PDFs stay light: only the pages near the screen are drawn.
  • No external services, no tracking and no cookies. PDFs are opened directly from your site.

Built on PDF.js

The viewer uses PDF.js by Mozilla, the same PDF engine used in Firefox, included in the plugin.

Source code

The PDF engine is PDF.js 6.5.438 by Mozilla, licensed under the Apache License 2.0, included unminified in vendor/pdfjs/ with its JavaScript image decoders. Fonts that are not embedded in a PDF are shown with the visitor’s system fonts. Source: https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Toolszu PDF Embedder”, then click Install Now and Activate.
  2. Edit a post, add the PDF Viewer block and choose your PDF.
  3. Optional: go to Settings > Toolszu PDF to set the default height, zoom, toolbar buttons and theme, and to turn on the “Save as PDF” button.
sections.faq:
Can I show a PDF from another website?

Only if that website allows it (this is called CORS). Many sites do not, and then the viewer shows a link to open the PDF instead. To be sure it works, upload the PDF to your Media Library.

Can I stop people from downloading my PDF?

You can hide the Download, Print and Open buttons. But anyone who can see a PDF can still save it, so do not publish files that must stay private.

Does it work on phones?

Yes. The toolbar adapts to small screens, pages fit the screen width, and full screen also works on iPhone.

How do I change the size of one viewer?

Select the block and change the height in the block settings on the right. With the shortcode, add height="600px" or height="90vh".

Which shortcode options are there?

[toolszu_pdf url=”…” title=”…” height=”800px” zoom=”page-width” page=”3″ download=”no” print=”no” search=”no” sidebar=”no” zoombar=”no” fullscreen=”no” open=”no”]

Does “Save as PDF” create the PDF on my server?

No. It uses the browser’s own “Save as PDF” option in the print window, so it works on every host and costs no server resources.

Will it slow down my site?

No. Nothing loads on pages without a PDF, and on pages with one, the PDF engine waits until the viewer is about to appear on screen.
